title: I built a Blender addon to separate, repair and retopologize AI-generated meshes
author: adrien_flex
selftext:
I know not everyone here does their own 3D modeling, but this might be useful to some of you.

I recently shared my golem workflow here, going from a character design to a 3D model and then into Godot. Thanks for all the discussion on that post.

I've also been working on tools to separate fused parts and rebuild the topology of dense meshes. I'm a 3D character artist, and I've spent the last few weeks developing Nitro Retopo, a segmentation and retopology addon for Blender.

You draw boundaries directly on the surface, separate the parts you want to work on, repair them and draw new topology. The goal is to get a clean mesh you can edit more precisely, unwrap and texture. For this first demo, I used an AI-generated knight.

I developed the addon with substantial help from AI coding tools, shaping and testing the workflow around my own projects. There's still work involved in preparing a character for a game, especially for animation, but these tools help with the cleanup and retopology stages.

It's a paid addon, available on SuperHive:  
[https://superhivemarket.com/products/nitro-retopo](https://superhivemarket.com/products/nitro-retopo)

comments.author: superkickstart
comments.body:
Nice work.

What makes this different from let's say retopoflow or speedretopo?

replies.author: adrien_flex
replies.body: Thanks! The main idea is to divide the existing surface into patches instead of building them one by one. Each new cut can split several patches at once, so a few strokes can define a whole region. Each patch side has exactly four segments, so neighboring patches fit together. You then choose how the topology flows inside each patch.

comments.author: CycleMother2006
comments.body: This has a ton of potential. I think shrinkwrapping shit topology is faster, but I don't think i've ever had a cleanly wrapped model that didn't require a huge amount of remodeling to get the shape properly fixed afterward. It seems like this maintains the shape? Is it one for one, or just approximate? If exact that's crazy. How does it fair with simple, solid assets? Something less complex than a gun. Like if I were to take this to a refrigerator or microwave? I fall asleep when modeling simple assets, but I also don't want to waste 2000 polys on a mostly box-shaped oven or fridge, however most tools aren't particularly good at determining the amount of polys actually needed... or is the poly count manually set for every region?

replies.author: adrien_flex
replies.body:
Thanks! Each vertex is placed on the sculpt’s surface. You can still lose some volume between vertices if you go very low-poly, but with enough geometry it usually follows the shape well.

It could work on something like a fridge or microwave, though very angular shapes need precise patch placement to get a regular result. For a simple box-shaped asset, traditional modeling might be more practical.

comments.author: joeld42
comments.body: Is there a free trial or a demonstration video? I would insta-buy this if it worked, but so many of these types of tools look great in gifs but fall down when I try them on real meshes?

replies.author: joeld42
replies.body:
I went ahead and bought it. It works but it a liitle hard to use. My main complaint was not being able to move the camera in draw mode. It would be nice if you could draw the whole curve network before it knifed it, or adjust curve handles. I'd much rather be able to lay out the patches and then fine tune the placement of the corners and seams but it's still way easier than doing it by hand. Would also be nice to have a "shortest path" mode for drawing the cuts that didn't knife things, for when a seam was in a crevice or something, but I can still mark those by hand. I think the best thing was that it works with the regular "mark seam" tools, so I can still go ahead and hand-adjust weird corners and stuff. 

Haven't tried a whole model yet, just playing with it but it seems good so far. I'll try it on a bigger mesh tonight.

replies.author: SlashForward
replies.body: Thanks for this update, I would be interested in hearing how it was with the bigger mesh for you.

replies.author: adrien_flex
replies.body:
Thanks for buying it and sharing your feedback! 😄  
I’m recording a more detailed tutorial covering the tools and techniques. The addon is in active development, so feedback like yours really helps shape the next improvements.

I’m also making major improvements to the Simplify brush, which rebuilds small problem areas with simpler triangles to make them easier to cut.

I’ve noted your shortest-path suggestion, that’s an interesting idea. Rotating the view in Draw Mode is currently a limitation, but I’ll keep it in mind and look into what’s possible.

I’d also love to hear how it goes with the bigger mesh!
